title: 6 Ways a Christian Husband Cherishes His Wife
author: Le Ann Trees
summary: Le Ann Trees addresses the misuse of Ephesians 5 as a license for husbands to mistreat their wives, arguing that the passage instead lays a heavy responsibility on the husband. She briefly examines the Greek terms for submit and respect to show that a wife's submission recognizes an ordered structure rather than an obligation to endure abuse. The article then sets out six things a Christian husband owes his wife: love, respect, spiritual leadership, attention, devotion and enjoyment, each grounded in a short scriptural rationale. The move is to reframe headship as sacrificial care, in which the husband's personal happiness is subordinated to loving his wife as Christ loved the church. The piece is an updated republication of an earlier Core Christianity article.
points: Trees argues that Paul's call for wives to submit does not require them to endure abuse, neglect or mistreatment of any kind.
Headship is recast as responsibility, including overseeing the spiritual training of the family even when the wife is well equipped in doctrine.
A husband is called to set aside substantial time to enjoy his wife's company and seek to understand her better.
In hard seasons, the article says, a husband's personal happiness must be subordinated to sacrificially loving his wife.
quotes: While some Christians have wrongly used these Bible verses as an excuse for husbands to mistreat their wives, the verses actually communicate the vast responsibility a husband has to care for his wife and the wife’s duty to honor her husband
He should do his best to “nurture and cherish” his wife in the love of Christ as he would his own flesh and tend to her spiritual, emotional, intellectual, and physical needs

When Paul tells wives to submit to their husbands in Ephesians 5:24, he does not mean that wives must endure abuse, neglect, or mistreatment of any kind by their husbands. Rather, Paul is reminding the church that a wife is under the leadership of her husband

Even though his wife may be well equipped in biblical doctrine and application and spend a considerable amount of time instructing their children in the faith, a husband must be diligent to oversee and guide the spiritual training of his family
He should always do his best to set aside a substantial amount of time to be with his wife, enjoy her company, and seek to understand her better.

Even when times are difficult due to financial, emotional, or physical challenges, a husband’s personal happiness must always be subordinated to sacrificially loving his wife “as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her

She is a precious gift from God given to comfort, support, encourage, and love him (Prov. 18:22; 31:10–12; 1 Pet. 3:1). The more a husband values, cherishes, and nurtures his wife, the more she will reflect God’s love as his radiant bride.
